name: Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd al-Thumālī al-Azdī
summary: The head of the Basran school in Baghdad, author of al-Muqtaḍab and al-Kāmil, and rival of the Kufan Thaʿlab: their two circles made Baghdad the city of grammar.
bio: Al-Mubarrad was born in Basra around 210/826 and learnt with al-Jarmī and al-Māzinī, reading al-Kitāb with both. He went to the court of al-Mutawakkil in Samarra and, after the caliph's murder in 247/861, to Baghdad, where he stayed until his death.

Al-Zubaydī tells how he made his name there. He arrived poor and unknown, and after the Friday prayer began to explain grammar aloud as if someone had asked him, until a circle gathered. Thaʿlab, the head of the Kufans, sent two of his students, al-Zajjāj and Ibn al-Ḥāʾik, to break it up. Al-Zajjāj asked a question; al-Mubarrad answered it, then refuted his own answer, then set the first answer right again, and did the same through fourteen questions. Al-Zajjāj told his companions to go back to their teacher without him: 'I speak of knowledge and reasoning, not of fame.' He became al-Mubarrad's student, paying him an allowance for his lessons.

From then on the two masters taught side by side, and their rivalry is a theme of every ṭabaqāt; al-Zubaydī reports that Thaʿlab was as sparing of words as al-Mubarrad, and wider in learning, but answered by hints where al-Mubarrad asked and answered plainly. Al-Mubarrad's al-Muqtaḍab is a full grammar on Sībawayh's lines, and al-Kāmil a book of language and letters still read; he also wrote a critique of Sībawayh, al-Radd ʿalā Sībawayh. Al-Zajjāj, Ibn al-Sarrāj, al-Akhfash al-Aṣghar, Ibn Durustawayh and Nifṭawayh were among his students. He died in Baghdad in 285/898 or 286/899.

works.title: al-Radd ʿalā Sībawayh
works.note: Answered later by Ibn Wallād in al-Intiṣār.

uncertain: The meaning of his nickname, al-Mubarrad ('the cooled') or al-Mubarrid ('who sets right'), is explained in several ways, some of them jokes of his rivals.

sources.title: al-Zubaydī, Ṭabaqāt al-naḥwiyyīn wa-l-lughawiyyīn, entry 36 (Arabic text, OpenITI)
